definition_zh: 喂养；进食；供应；饲料；信息流
definition_en: to give food to, to eat, to supply something, food for animals, or a stream of online posts
core_image: 天刚亮，农妇提着一桶谷子走向鸡舍，鸡群立刻围了上来
scene: 天刚亮，农妇就提着桶去喂鸡。She went out to feed the chickens at dawn.
sceneCN: 这里 feed 是「喂养」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她天亮时出去喂鸡。

senses.title: To give food
senses.definition: to give food to a person or animal
senses.definitionCN: 给人或动物食物
senses.example: Farmers feed the animals before sunrise.
senses.exampleCN: 农民在日出前喂养牲畜。
senses.why: This is the basic everyday sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最基本的日常义。

senses.title: To eat
senses.definition: to eat, especially for a baby or an animal
senses.definitionCN: 进食，尤指婴儿或动物
senses.example: The baby feeds every three hours.
senses.exampleCN: 婴儿每三小时吃一次奶。
senses.why: The same verb describes the one taking food.
senses.whyCN: 同一个动词也可描述进食的一方。

senses.title: To supply or channel
senses.definition: to supply something continuously into a system
senses.definitionCN: 持续向某个系统供应或输入
senses.example: The river feeds water into the reservoir.
senses.exampleCN: 这条河把水送入水库。
senses.why: Food going in becomes any material going in.
senses.whyCN: 食物进入引申为任何物质进入。

senses.title: Animal food
senses.definition: food prepared for farm animals
senses.definitionCN: 为农场牲畜准备的食物
senses.example: We bought a bag of chicken feed.
senses.exampleCN: 我们买了一袋鸡饲料。
senses.why: The verb turns into a noun for what is given.
senses.whyCN: 动词转化为表示被喂之物的名词。

senses.title: A stream of posts
senses.definition: a continuously updated stream of content online
senses.definitionCN: 网络上持续更新的内容流
senses.example: Her news feed was full of travel photos.
senses.exampleCN: 她的信息流里全是旅行照片。
senses.why: Digital content flows in like material through a channel.
senses.whyCN: 数字内容像物质一样通过通道流入。

intro.en: Feed goes back to Old English fēdan and a Germanic root for food.
intro.cn: feed 可追溯到古英语 fēdan，出自表示食物的日耳曼语词根。

items.en: The root fōdijan meant to give food.
items.cn: 词根 fōdijan 意为给食物。

items.en: Fēdan meant to give food or nourish.
items.cn: fēdan 意为给食物或滋养。

items.en: The verb was spelled fede.
items.cn: 动词拼作 fede。

items.en: Feed also came to mean supply or channel.
items.cn: feed 又表示供应或输送。

items.en: Computing added the sense of a content stream.
items.cn: 计算机领域又增加了「内容流」的义项。

note.en: Feed is compared with similar-looking words and with words for supplying food.
note.cn: 把 feed 与形近词以及表示供给食物的词作比较。

entries.definition: to give food needed for life

normalIntro.en: Feed means to give food, to eat, to supply, the food itself, or an online stream.
normalIntro.cn: feed 意为喂食、进食、供应、饲料，或网络信息流。

normal.en: Feed the dog is a common morning task.
normal.cn: feed the dog 是常见的早晨任务。

normal.en: Animals that feed on grass are herbivores.
normal.cn: 以草为食的动物是食草动物。

normal.en: Data feeds into the computer from many sensors.
normal.cn: 数据从许多传感器输入计算机。

normal.en: Be fed up with means to be very annoyed.
normal.cn: be fed up with 意为非常厌烦。

normal.en: A news feed keeps updating all day.
normal.cn: 新闻信息流整天不断更新。

abstract.en: Feeding is the oldest way of connecting one life to another.
abstract.cn: 喂养是一个生命连接另一个生命的最古老方式。

abstract.en: Anything that flows into a system can be called a feed.
abstract.cn: 任何流入系统的东西都可以称为 feed。

abstract.en: We now feed on information as much as on bread.
abstract.cn: 如今我们既靠面包，也靠信息而活。

examples.en: Farmers feed the animals before sunrise.
examples.cn: 农民在日出前喂养牲畜。

examples.en: The baby feeds every three hours.
examples.cn: 婴儿每三小时吃一次奶。

examples.en: She was fed up with the noise.
examples.cn: 她受够了那噪音。

dict_mnemonic.text: feed 源自古英语 fēdan（给食物），与 food 同源，核心是「把食物送进去」。

root: 源自古英语 fēdan（给食物），出自日耳曼语词根 fōdijan，核心义「供给养分」。

sensesIntro.en: Feed means to give food, to eat, to supply, animal food, or a stream of online content.
sensesIntro.cn: feed 意为喂食、进食、供应、饲料，或网络内容流。

core.en: Putting something in so that another can grow or work.
core.cn: 把某物送入，使另一方得以生长或运转。

branches.en: To give food to someone.
To take food, especially as a baby.
To supply material into a system.
Food prepared for animals.
A stream of online content.

intro.en: Feed forms words for feeders, supplies, and ways of giving too much or too little.
intro.cn: feed 构成表示饲养者、供给以及过多过少喂食的词。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic, so Latin entries are not its direct source.
latinIntro.cn: 该词属日耳曼语，拉丁条目并非其直接来源。

items.example: She feeds the birds every day.
He feeds the fish twice a day.
They fed the horses at dawn.

items.meaning: a person or device that feeds
items.example: The bird feeder hangs by the window.

items.exampleCN: 老师给出了有用的反馈。

items.example: The plant turns feedstock into fuel.
items.exampleCN: 这家工厂把原料变成燃料。
养分不足的植物长得慢。

definition_zh: 反馈；反馈意见；（电子）回授
definition_en: comments on how well something works, information returned by a system, or a return of part of an electronic signal
core_image: 试讲结束后，同事们把写满建议的纸一张张递到他手里
scene: 试讲结束后，同事们逐条写下建议交给他。The teacher welcomed feedback from her students.
sceneCN: 这里 feedback 是「反馈意见」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这位老师欢迎学生们的反馈。

senses.title: Comments on performance
senses.definition: comments about how well someone or something has done
senses.definitionCN: 关于某人或某事表现如何的意见
senses.example: The teacher gave feedback on each essay.
senses.exampleCN: 老师对每篇作文都给出了反馈。
senses.why: This is the everyday sense in learning and work.
senses.whyCN: 这是学习与工作中最常见的含义。

senses.title: Information from a system
senses.definition: information about the result of a process, used to adjust it
senses.definitionCN: 关于过程结果、用于调整该过程的信息
senses.example: The system uses feedback to adjust the temperature.
senses.exampleCN: 系统利用反馈来调节温度。
senses.why: Machines return information the way people return comments.
senses.whyCN: 机器返回信息，正如人返回意见。

senses.title: Electronic return
senses.definition: the return of part of an output signal to the input
senses.definitionCN: 把部分输出信号送回输入端
senses.example: Too much feedback caused a loud howl.
senses.exampleCN: 过强的回授引起了刺耳的啸叫。
senses.why: Audio equipment made the term famous.
senses.whyCN: 音响设备让这个术语广为人知。

intro.en: Feedback is an English compound of feed and back, first used in control engineering.
intro.cn: feedback 是 feed 与 back 的英语复合词，最初用于控制工程。

items.en: Fēdan meant to give food or supply.
items.cn: fēdan 意为给食物或供应。

items.en: Bæc meant the back or backward direction.
items.cn: bæc 意为背部或向后方向。

items.en: Engineers named the return of a signal feedback.
items.cn: 工程师把信号的返回称为 feedback。

items.en: The word spread to systems of control and communication.
items.cn: 该词扩展到控制与通信系统。

items.en: Feedback became common for comments on performance.
items.cn: feedback 成为表示表现评价的常用词。

note.en: Feedback is compared with similar-looking words and with words for responses.
note.cn: 把 feedback 与形近词以及表示回应的词作比较。

entries.definition: a bag of food for an animal

normalIntro.en: Feedback is information fed back to the source so it can improve.
normalIntro.cn: feedback 是送回源头、帮助其改进的信息。

normal.en: Feedback is literally fed back to the sender.
normal.cn: feedback 字面上就是把信息「喂回」发送者。

normal.en: Positive feedback encourages more of the same.
normal.cn: 正面反馈会鼓励继续做同样的事。

normal.en: A feedback loop keeps adjusting itself.
normal.cn: 反馈回路会不断自我调节。

normal.en: Customer feedback shapes better products.
normal.cn: 顾客反馈塑造更好的产品。

normal.en: In audio, feedback can become a loud howl.
normal.cn: 在音响中，回授可能变成刺耳啸叫。

abstract.en: Feedback closes the circle between action and result.
abstract.cn: 反馈把行动与结果连成一个圆。

abstract.en: A system without feedback cannot correct itself.
abstract.cn: 没有反馈的系统无法自我纠错。

abstract.en: Praise and criticism are both information.
abstract.cn: 赞扬与批评都是一种信息。

examples.en: The teacher gave feedback on each essay.
examples.cn: 老师对每篇作文都给出了反馈。

examples.en: The system uses feedback to adjust the temperature.
examples.cn: 系统利用反馈来调节温度。

examples.en: We need more feedback from customers.
examples.cn: 我们需要更多顾客反馈。

dict_mnemonic.text: feedback 由 feed（送入）与 back（返回）组合而成，字面是「送回的信息」，先用于工程，后用于日常评价。

root: 由 feed（送入）与 back（返回）构成的英语复合词，核心义「返回源头的信息」。

sensesIntro.en: Feedback means comments on performance, information returned by a system, or electronic signal return.
sensesIntro.cn: feedback 意为表现评价、系统返回的信息，或电子信号回授。

core.en: A return of information that lets a system or person adjust.
core.cn: 让系统或个人得以调整的信息回流。

branches.en: Comments that help people improve.
Information a system uses to adjust.
Part of a signal returning to the input.
People and machines both correct themselves with returned information.
branches.cn: 人与机器都依靠返回的信息自我修正。

branches.en: A howl in a microphone is feedback at its most literal.
branches.cn: 麦克风的啸叫是 feedback 最字面的形态。

intro.en: Feedback links the feed family with ideas of return and self-correction.
intro.cn: feedback 把 feed 词族与「返回、自我修正」的概念连接起来。

latinIntro.en: The word is a modern English compound, so Latin entries are not its direct source.
latinIntro.cn: 该词是现代英语复合词，拉丁条目并非其直接来源。

items.example: The lab recorded feedbacks from both systems.
items.exampleCN: 实验室记录了两个系统的反馈。

items.example: Sensors feed data to the computer.
items.exampleCN: 传感器向计算机输入数据。

items.example: The app feeds updates every minute.
items.exampleCN: 这个应用每分钟推送更新。

items.example: The feeding of data continues all night.

items.meaning: to feed power or data backward
items.example: The generator can backfeed the grid.
items.exampleCN: 发电机可以向电网反向馈电。
神经反馈用于训练注意力。
前馈可以提前防止错误。

definition_zh: 感觉；觉得；触摸；手感
definition_en: to experience a feeling or sensation, to think or believe, to touch, or the texture of something
core_image: 他伸手摸了摸口袋，确认钥匙还在，指尖碰到冰凉的金属
scene: 他伸手摸了摸口袋，确认钥匙还在。He felt the key in his pocket.
sceneCN: 这里 feel 是「触摸」（第 3 个义项）；句意：他摸到了口袋里的钥匙。

senses.title: To experience a sensation
senses.definition: to experience a physical or emotional sensation
senses.definitionCN: 体验身体或情绪上的感受
senses.example: I feel tired after the long walk.
senses.exampleCN: 长途步行后我感到疲倦。
senses.why: This is the broad sense of inner experience.
senses.whyCN: 这是内在感受的宽泛义。

senses.title: To think or believe
senses.definition: to have an opinion or belief about something
senses.definitionCN: 对某事持有看法或信念
senses.example: I feel that the plan will work.
senses.exampleCN: 我觉得这个计划行得通。
senses.why: Inner sense extends to judgment.
senses.whyCN: 内在感受延伸到判断。

senses.title: To touch
senses.definition: to touch something in order to learn about it
senses.definitionCN: 通过触摸来了解某物
senses.example: She felt the fabric to check its quality.
senses.exampleCN: 她摸了摸布料来检查质量。
senses.why: Feeling with the hand is the physical origin.
senses.whyCN: 用手触摸是该词的身体来源。

senses.title: Texture or impression
senses.definition: the way something feels when touched, or a general impression
senses.definitionCN: 某物被触摸时的感觉，或总体印象
senses.example: The room has a warm, soft feel.
senses.exampleCN: 这个房间有一种温暖柔和的感觉。
senses.why: The verb turns into a noun for the quality sensed.
senses.whyCN: 动词转化为名词，表示被感知的性质。

intro.en: Feel goes back to Old English fēlan and a Germanic root for touching or sensing.
intro.cn: feel 可追溯到古英语 fēlan，出自表示触摸或感知的日耳曼语词根。

items.en: The root fōlijan meant to sense or perceive.
items.cn: 词根 fōlijan 意为感觉或察觉。

items.en: Fēlan meant to touch or perceive.
items.cn: fēlan 意为触摸或感知。

items.en: Felen added the sense of emotional experience.
items.cn: felen 增加了情绪体验的意思。

items.en: Feel came to mean believe or have an opinion.
items.cn: feel 开始表示相信或有看法。

items.en: The noun feel names texture and atmosphere.
items.cn: 名词 feel 表示质感与氛围。

note.en: Feel is compared with similar-looking words and with words for sensing.
note.cn: 把 feel 与形近词以及表示感受的词作比较。

entries.definition: to put the hand on something
to become aware through the senses

normalIntro.en: Feel covers inner sensation, opinion, touching, and the texture you sense.
normalIntro.cn: feel 涵盖内在感觉、看法、触摸以及感知到的质感。

normal.en: Feel like can mean want or seem.
normal.cn: feel like 既可表示「想要」，也可表示「像」。

normal.en: Feel free means go ahead without hesitation.
normal.cn: feel free 意为尽管去做。

normal.en: Feel about asks for someone's opinion.
normal.cn: feel about 用来询问某人的看法。

normal.en: A feel for a subject comes with practice.
normal.cn: 对一门学科的感觉来自练习。

normal.en: Felt is the past form of feel.
normal.cn: felt 是 feel 的过去式。

abstract.en: Touch is how the body knows the world; feeling is how the mind knows it.
abstract.cn: 触摸是身体认识世界的方式，感受是心灵认识世界的方式。

abstract.en: We say we feel an idea when it has reached the body.
abstract.cn: 当一个想法抵达身体时，我们说自己「觉得」它。

abstract.en: The feel of a place is made of many small senses.
abstract.cn: 一个地方的感觉由许多细小感受构成。

examples.en: I feel tired after the long walk.
examples.cn: 长途步行后我感到疲倦。

examples.en: She felt the fabric to check its quality.
examples.cn: 她摸了摸布料来检查质量。

examples.en: The room has a warm, soft feel.
examples.cn: 这个房间有一种温暖柔和的感觉。

dict_mnemonic.text: feel 源自古英语 fēlan（触摸、感知），词义从「用手摸」扩展到内心的感觉与看法。

root: 源自古英语 fēlan（触摸、感知），出自日耳曼语词根，核心义「通过感官或内心察觉」。

sensesIntro.en: Feel means to experience a sensation, believe something, touch something, or the texture felt.
sensesIntro.cn: feel 意为感受、认为、触摸，或被感知到的手感。

core.en: Awareness through the body or the mind.
core.cn: 通过身体或心灵获得的觉察。

branches.en: A physical or emotional sensation.
A belief or opinion held inside.
The act of touching to learn.
The quality something has when touched.
What we sense and what we believe blend into one word.
branches.cn: 我们感到的与我们相信的融合在同一个词里。

intro.en: Feel forms words for sensation, sensitivity, and lack of feeling.
intro.cn: feel 构成表示感觉、敏感与缺乏感情之词的词。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic, so Latin entries are not its direct source.
latinIntro.cn: 该词属日耳曼语，拉丁条目并非其直接来源。

items.example: I feel cold near the window.
A feeling of calm filled the room.
items.exampleCN: 房间里充满了平静的感觉。
他无情的回答伤害了她。

items.example: She spoke feelingly about her home.

items.exampleCN: 那是一部让人心情愉快的电影。

definition_zh: 同伴；家伙；团体成员；研究员
definition_en: a companion, a man, a member of a group, or an academic researcher
core_image: 同行的旅伴拍了拍他的肩，示意前面就是客栈的灯笼
scene: 同行的旅伴拍了拍他的肩，示意前面就是客栈。His fellow traveller pointed to the inn ahead.
sceneCN: 这里 fellow 是「同伴」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他的旅伴指向前面的客栈。

senses.title: A companion
senses.definition: a person who shares an activity or journey with you
senses.definitionCN: 与你共同活动或旅行的人
senses.example: A fellow student lent me his notes.
senses.exampleCN: 一位同学把他的笔记借给了我。
senses.why: This is the oldest and most central sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老、最核心的义项。

senses.title: A man or person
senses.definition: an informal word for a man or person
senses.definitionCN: 对男性或人的非正式称呼
senses.example: He is a friendly fellow.
senses.exampleCN: 他是个友好的人。
senses.why: Companion sense softened into a casual word for a person.
senses.whyCN: 同伴义软化为对人的随意称呼。

senses.title: A member of a group
senses.definition: a member of a society, college, or group
senses.definitionCN: 学会、学院或团体的成员
senses.example: The fellows met once a month.
senses.exampleCN: 成员们每月聚会一次。
senses.why: Equal companions became organized members.
senses.whyCN: 平等的同伴关系发展为有组织的成员身份。

senses.title: An academic researcher
senses.definition: a senior researcher at a university or college
senses.definitionCN: 大学或学院中的高级研究人员
senses.example: She became a research fellow at the university.
senses.exampleCN: 她成了这所大学的研究员。
senses.why: A college fellow is a member of a learned community.
senses.whyCN: 大学 fellow 是学术共同体中的成员。

intro.en: Fellow came from Old Norse félagi, a partner who shares money or work.
intro.cn: fellow 来自古诺尔斯语 félagi，指共享钱财或工作的伙伴。

items.en: The root linked fē, money, with a partner.
items.cn: 该词根把表示钱财的 fē 与伙伴联系起来。

items.en: Félagi meant a partner or comrade.
items.cn: félagi 意为伙伴或同伴。

items.en: Felawe meant a companion or associate.
items.cn: felawe 意为同伴或同事。

items.en: Fellow also became a word for a man.
items.cn: fellow 也成为表示人的词。

items.en: Universities adopted fellow for senior researchers.
items.cn: 大学采用 fellow 指高级研究员。

note.en: Fellow is compared with similar-looking words and with words for companions.
note.cn: 把 fellow 与形近词以及表示同伴的词作比较。

entries.definition: a person who travels with another
a close companion, especially in a group
a person who shares an activity

normalIntro.en: A fellow is a companion, a casual word for a man, a group member, or a researcher.
normalIntro.cn: fellow 是同伴、对人的随意称呼、团体成员，或研究员。

normal.en: Fellow student means a student like you.
normal.cn: fellow student 指与你身份相同的同学。

normal.en: A good fellow is a friendly and decent man.
normal.cn: a good fellow 指友好正派的人。

normal.en: Fellowship can mean friendship or a funded position.
normal.cn: fellowship 既可指友谊，也可指奖学金职位。

normal.en: Research fellow is a common academic title.
normal.cn: research fellow 是常见的学术头衔。

normal.en: Fellow and follow differ in the final letters.
normal.cn: fellow 与 follow 在结尾字母上不同。

abstract.en: A fellow was originally someone who shared money.
abstract.cn: fellow 最初指共享钱财的人。

abstract.en: Sharing a path is enough to make two people fellows.
abstract.cn: 共走一条路就足以让两个人成为同伴。

abstract.en: A community is many fellows who agree to belong.
abstract.cn: 共同体就是许多同意归属的成员。

examples.en: A fellow student lent me his notes.
examples.cn: 一位同学把他的笔记借给了我。

examples.en: He is a friendly fellow.
examples.cn: 他是个友好的人。

examples.en: She became a research fellow at the university.
examples.cn: 她成了这所大学的研究员。

dict_mnemonic.text: fellow 来自古诺尔斯语 félagi（共享钱财的伙伴），由「合伙人」扩展为「同伴、成员、研究员」。

root: 源自古诺尔斯语 félagi（合伙人），与「钱财、共同持有」有关，核心义「共享某事的同伴」。

sensesIntro.en: Fellow means a companion, a man, a member of a group, or a senior academic researcher.
sensesIntro.cn: fellow 意为同伴、男性或人、团体成员，或高级研究员。

core.en: Someone who shares a path, a group, or a purpose with you.
core.cn: 与你共享道路、团体或目标的人。

branches.en: A companion on a journey or task.
A casual word for a man.
A member of an organized group.
A researcher in a learned community.
branches.cn: 学术共同体中的研究人员。

branches.en: Companionship and membership both mean belonging together.
branches.cn: 同伴关系与成员身份都意味着彼此归属。

intro.en: Fellow forms words for companionship, shared feeling, and academic positions.
intro.cn: fellow 构成表示同伴关系、共同感受与学术职位的词。

latinIntro.en: The word came from Old Norse, so Latin entries are not its direct source.
latinIntro.cn: 该词来自古诺尔斯语，拉丁条目并非其直接来源。

items.example: He is a fellow of the society.
The fellows shared a long table.

items.meaning: friendship or a funded academic post

items.exampleCN: 这所学院提供三个研究员职位。

items.example: We should care for our fellowman.
He worked for the good of his fellowmen.
items.exampleCN: 他为同胞的福祉而工作。

items.example: He felt a fellow-feeling for the newcomer.
items.exampleCN: 他对新来者产生了同感。

items.meaning: a person on the same journey
items.example: Her fellow traveller spoke little English.
items.exampleCN: 她的旅伴几乎不会说英语。

definition_zh: 女性的；雌性的；女性；雌性动物
definition_en: of the sex that can bear young, a woman or girl, or a female animal
core_image: 花园里那只雌孔雀没有开屏，却安静地立在栅栏边
scene: 花园里那只雌孔雀没有开屏，却安静地立在栅栏边。The female peacock stood quietly by the fence.
sceneCN: 这里 female 是「雌性的」（第 2 个义项）；句意：那只雌孔雀安静地站在栅栏边。

senses.title: Of women
senses.definition: of or relating to women or girls
senses.definitionCN: 与女性或女孩有关的
senses.example: The female engineer led the team.
senses.exampleCN: 那位女工程师带领团队。
senses.why: This is the human use of the adjective.
senses.whyCN: 这是该形容词用于人类的义项。

senses.title: Of female animals
senses.definition: of the sex in animals that produces eggs
senses.definitionCN: 动物中产卵的性别
senses.example: A female bird builds the nest here.
senses.exampleCN: 在这里，雌鸟负责筑巢。
senses.why: Biology uses the word across species.
senses.whyCN: 生物学用该词指各个物种。

senses.title: A woman or female animal
senses.definition: a person or animal of the female sex
senses.definitionCN: 女性的人或雌性动物
senses.example: The audience was mostly female.
senses.exampleCN: 观众大多是女性。
senses.why: The adjective also stands alone as a noun.
senses.whyCN: 该形容词也可单独作名词使用。

intro.en: Female comes from Latin femella, a young woman, a small form of femina, woman.
intro.cn: female 源自拉丁语 femella（年轻女子），是 femina（女人）的指小形式。

items.en: Femina meant a woman.
items.cn: femina 意为女人。

items.en: Femella meant a young woman.
items.cn: femella 意为年轻女子。

items.en: Femelle named a female animal.
items.cn: femelle 指雌性动物。

items.en: Female entered English with a spelling changed by folk memory of male.
items.cn: female 进入英语，拼写受到 male 一词的民间联想影响。

items.en: The word now describes people, animals, and connectors.
items.cn: 现代英语中该词可形容人、动物与接口。

note.en: Female is compared with similar-looking words and with words for women.
note.cn: 把 female 与形近词以及表示女性的词作比较。

entries.definition: of the sex that does not bear young
a polite word for a woman

normalIntro.en: Female describes women and egg-producing animals, and can stand as a noun.
normalIntro.cn: female 形容女性与产卵的动物，也可单独作名词。

normal.en: Female and male are a natural pair.
normal.cn: female 与 male 是一对自然的对应词。

normal.en: The word is not spelled with a hyphen.
normal.cn: 这个词的拼写中没有连字符。

normal.en: Female can describe people, animals, and even plugs.
normal.cn: female 可形容人、动物，甚至插接口。

normal.en: Feminine describes qualities, while female describes sex.
normal.cn: feminine 描述气质，female 描述性别。

normal.en: Femaleness names the state of being female.
normal.cn: femaleness 指女性的状态。

abstract.en: The spelling changed to match male, though the roots differ.
abstract.cn: 拼写为配合 male 而改变，尽管两者词源不同。

abstract.en: A word for sex also became a word for social roles.
abstract.cn: 表示性别的词也变成了表示社会角色的词。

abstract.en: Naming sex is simple; naming its meaning is not.
abstract.cn: 指出性别很简单，解释其意义却不容易。

examples.en: The female engineer led the team.
examples.cn: 那位女工程师带领团队。

examples.en: A female bird builds the nest here.
examples.cn: 在这里，雌鸟负责筑巢。

examples.en: The audience was mostly female.
examples.cn: 观众大多是女性。

dict_mnemonic.text: female 源自拉丁语 femella（年轻女子），拼写后来受 male 影响，但两者并无共同词源。

root: 源自拉丁语 femina（女人）的指小形式 femella，核心义「女性或雌性」。

sensesIntro.en: Female means of women, of egg-producing animals, or a woman or female animal.
sensesIntro.cn: female 意为女性的、雌性的，或女性与雌性动物。

core.en: The sex that bears young, applied to people and animals.
core.cn: 能孕育后代的性别，适用于人与动物。

branches.en: The adjective for women and girls.
branches.cn: 形容女性与女孩的形容词。

branches.en: The adjective for egg-producing animals.
branches.cn: 形容产卵动物的形容词。

branches.en: A noun for a woman or female animal.
branches.cn: 表示女性或雌性动物的名词。

branches.en: The adjective and noun both name female people.
branches.cn: 形容词与名词都可指女性。

branches.en: In biology the noun is used across species.
branches.cn: 在生物学中该名词跨物种使用。

intro.en: Female belongs to the femina family, which also gives feminine and feminist.
intro.cn: female 属于 femina 词族，同族还有 feminine 与 feminist。

latinIntro.en: Latin femina and femella are the historical sources.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 femina 与 femella 是历史来源。

items.example: The study measured neither femaleness nor maleness.
items.exampleCN: 这项研究既不测量女性特质也不测量男性特质。

items.example: The room has a feminine style.
items.exampleCN: 这个房间有女性化的风格。

items.example: She refused to define femininity for others.
items.exampleCN: 她拒绝替别人定义女性气质。
女权主义改变了许多法律。
她是一位知名的女权主义者。

items.example: The design feminizes the old uniform.
items.exampleCN: 这个设计让旧制服更具女性风格。

items.example: The feminization of the profession happened slowly.
items.exampleCN: 这一职业的女性化过程发生得很缓慢。

definition_zh: 栅栏；围栏；击剑；收赃
definition_en: a barrier around a field or garden, the sport of fighting with swords, or to buy and sell stolen goods
core_image: 木栅栏沿着草坡延伸，风吹过时轻轻作响
scene: 院子四周立着一圈木栅栏，风吹过时轻轻作响。A wooden fence surrounds the garden.
sceneCN: 这里 fence 是「栅栏」（第 1 个义项）；句意：一圈木栅栏围着花园。

senses.title: Barrier around land
senses.definition: a barrier of wood, wire, or metal around a field or garden
senses.definitionCN: 围住田地或花园的木、铁丝或金属障碍物
senses.example: A wooden fence surrounds the garden.
senses.exampleCN: 一圈木栅栏围着花园。
senses.why: This is the everyday sense of an enclosure.
senses.whyCN: 这是表示「围合障碍」的日常义。

senses.title: Sport with swords
senses.definition: the sport of fighting with long thin swords
senses.definitionCN: 用细长剑进行的体育运动
senses.example: She trains in fencing twice a week.
senses.exampleCN: 她每周练两次击剑。
senses.why: Fencing is the noun of the sword sport.
senses.whyCN: fencing 是击剑运动的名称。

senses.title: Enclose with a fence
senses.definition: to put a fence around an area
senses.definitionCN: 在某片区域周围设置栅栏
senses.example: They fenced the field to keep sheep in.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把田地围起来以免羊跑出去。
senses.why: The noun supplies a verb for enclosing.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为表示「围起来」的动词。

senses.title: Deal in stolen goods
senses.definition: to buy and sell property that was stolen
senses.definitionCN: 买卖偷来的财物
senses.example: He was arrested for fencing stolen bikes.
senses.exampleCN: 他因收售赃车被捕。
senses.why: The criminal sense is older than it looks.
senses.whyCN: 这个犯罪义比看上去更古老。

intro.en: Fence is a shortened form of defence, from Latin defendere, to ward off.
intro.cn: fence 是 defence 的缩略形式，出自拉丁语 defendere（挡开）。

items.en: Defendere meant to ward off or protect.
items.cn: defendere 意为挡开、保护。

items.en: Defens meant defence or protection.
items.cn: defens 意为防御、保护。

items.en: Fens was shortened from defens.
items.cn: fens 由 defens 缩略而来。

items.en: The word came to mean a barrier and the sword sport.
items.cn: 该词逐渐指栅栏与击剑运动。

items.en: Criminals gave fence the sense of dealing in stolen goods.
items.cn: 犯罪圈给 fence 增添了买卖赃物的义项。

note.en: Fence is compared with similar-looking words and with words for barriers.
note.cn: 把 fence 与形近词以及表示障碍物的词作比较。

entries.definition: the sport of fighting with swords
a solid structure that encloses an area

normalIntro.en: Fence means a barrier, the sport of swords, or to trade stolen goods.
normalIntro.cn: fence 意为栅栏、击剑，或买卖赃物。

normal.en: Fence is a shortened defence.
normal.cn: fence 是 defence 的缩略形式。

normal.en: To sit on the fence is to avoid choosing a side.
normal.cn: sit on the fence 意为骑墙观望。

normal.en: Fencing is the sport, fence is the barrier.
normal.cn: fencing 是运动，fence 是栅栏。

normal.en: To fence a field is to enclose it.
normal.cn: fence a field 就是把田地围起来。

normal.en: A fence can also be a dealer in stolen goods.
normal.cn: fence 也可以指收赃的人。

abstract.en: Every fence marks where one place ends.
abstract.cn: 每一道栅栏都标出一处地方的边界。

abstract.en: A fence can protect or divide.
abstract.cn: 栅栏既能保护，也能分隔。

abstract.en: Some boundaries are built to be mended.
abstract.cn: 有些边界本就是为了修修补补而存在的。

examples.en: A wooden fence surrounds the garden.
examples.cn: 一圈木栅栏围着花园。

examples.en: They fenced the field to keep sheep in.
examples.cn: 他们把田地围起来以免羊跑出去。

examples.en: He was arrested for fencing stolen bikes.
examples.cn: 他因收售赃车被捕。

dict_mnemonic.text: fence 是 defence（防御）的缩略，先指防护设施，后指栅栏，再衍生出击剑与收赃等义。

root: 源自 defence（防御），出自拉丁语 defendere（挡开），核心义「挡在外面的围障」。

sensesIntro.en: Fence means a barrier, the sword sport, to enclose, or to trade stolen goods.
sensesIntro.cn: fence 意为栅栏、击剑、围起或收赃。

core.en: A barrier that keeps something in or out.
core.cn: 把某物挡在里面或外面的障碍。

branches.en: Wood or wire marks a boundary.
branches.cn: 木头或铁丝标出一条边界。

branches.en: Two people face off with thin swords.
A field is closed in.
Stolen property changes hands.
The noun and verb describe one barrier.
branches.cn: 名词与动词描述的是同一道围障。

intro.en: Fence connects to the Latin defendere family of protection words.
intro.cn: fence 与拉丁语 defendere（保护）这一词族相连。

latinIntro.en: Latin defendere and defensio are the historical base.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 defendere 与 defensio 是历史词根。

items.meaning: the sword sport or fence material

items.example: The walls are built for defence.
The team took a defensive position.

definition_zh: 节日；节庆；艺术节
definition_en: a special day or period of celebration, or a series of performances of music, film, or theatre
core_image: 街上挂满红灯笼，鼓声从巷口一路传过来
scene: 整条街挂起红灯笼，鼓声从巷口一路响过来。The whole town joins the spring festival.
sceneCN: 这里 festival 是「节日」（第 1 个义项）；句意：全城都参与了春节。

senses.title: Special day
senses.definition: a special day or period of religious or cultural celebration
senses.definitionCN: 宗教或文化庆祝的特殊日子或时期
senses.example: The whole town joins the spring festival.
senses.exampleCN: 全城都参与了春节。
senses.why: This is the broad calendar sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最宽泛的节庆日历义。

senses.title: Arts event
senses.definition: a series of performances of music, film, or theatre
senses.definitionCN: 一系列音乐、电影或戏剧演出
senses.example: The film festival lasts ten days.
senses.exampleCN: 电影节持续十天。
senses.why: Modern festivals gather artists and audiences.
senses.whyCN: 现代艺术节把艺术家与观众聚在一起。

senses.title: Merry celebration
senses.definition: a happy occasion of feasting and public enjoyment
senses.definitionCN: 宴饮与公众欢聚的喜庆场合
senses.example: The street was full of festival cheer.
senses.exampleCN: 街上洋溢着节庆的欢乐。
senses.why: The word can name the mood as well as the date.
senses.whyCN: 该词既指日期，也指那种气氛。

intro.en: Festival comes from Latin festum, a feast, through Old French festival.
intro.cn: festival 源自拉丁语 festum（宴庆），经古法语 festival 传入英语。

items.en: Festum meant a feast or holy day.
items.cn: festum 意为宴庆、圣日。

items.en: Festivus meant joyful or festive.
items.cn: festivus 意为欢乐的、节庆的。

items.en: Festival named a feast day.
items.cn: festival 指宴庆之日。

items.en: English festival kept the religious sense.
items.cn: 英语 festival 保留宗教节日的含义。

items.en: The word spread to arts and community events.
items.cn: 该词扩展到艺术与社区活动。

note.en: Festival is compared with similar-looking words and with words for celebrations.
note.cn: 把 festival 与形近词以及表示庆祝的词作比较。

entries.definition: a joyful event for a special occasion
a public festival with music and costumes

normalIntro.en: Festival means a special day of celebration or a season of arts events.
normalIntro.cn: festival 意为特别的庆祝日或艺术活动季。

normal.en: Festival and feast share a Latin root.
normal.cn: festival 与 feast 共享拉丁词根。

normal.en: A film festival is a series of screenings.
normal.cn: 电影节是一系列放映活动。

normal.en: The spring festival marks the new year.
normal.cn: 春节标志新年的到来。

normal.en: The adjective is festive.
normal.cn: 形容词是 festive。

normal.en: Festivity means the joy of a festival.
normal.cn: festivity 指节庆的欢乐。

abstract.en: A festival is time set apart from ordinary days.
abstract.cn: 节日是从平常日子里划出来的一段时间。

abstract.en: Shared celebration makes a crowd into a community.
abstract.cn: 共同的庆祝把人群变成共同体。

abstract.en: Every festival remembers something older.
abstract.cn: 每个节日都在纪念更久远的东西。

examples.en: The whole town joins the spring festival.
examples.cn: 全城都参与了春节。

examples.en: The film festival lasts ten days.
examples.cn: 电影节持续十天。

examples.en: The street was full of festival cheer.
examples.cn: 街上洋溢着节庆的欢乐。

dict_mnemonic.text: festival 源自拉丁语 festum（宴庆），先指宗教节日，后泛指各类节庆与艺术节。

root: 源自拉丁语 festum（宴庆、圣日），核心义「指定用于欢庆的日子」。

sensesIntro.en: Festival means a special celebration day, an arts event, or a festive occasion.
sensesIntro.cn: festival 意为节日、艺术节或节庆场合。

core.en: Time set aside for celebration.
core.cn: 专门划出来用于庆祝的时间。

branches.en: A dated day of cultural celebration.
branches.cn: 有固定日期的文化庆祝日。

branches.en: A programmed season of performances.
The joy shared in the streets.
branches.cn: 在街头共享的欢乐气氛。

branches.en: A date and a mood carry one name.
branches.cn: 日期与气氛共用一个名称。

branches.en: Ancient and modern festivals both gather people.
branches.cn: 古今节日都把人们聚在一起。

intro.en: Festival belongs to the Latin festum family of feasting words.
intro.cn: festival 属于拉丁语 festum（宴庆）这一词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin festum and festivus are the historical base.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 festum 与 festivus 是历史词根。

items.example: The town holds two festivals a year.
items.exampleCN: 这座镇子一年办两个节庆。

items.example: The room had a festive air.
items.exampleCN: 房间里洋溢着节日气氛。

items.example: The festivity went on all night.
They prepared a feast for the guests.
items.exampleCN: 他们为客人准备了盛宴。

items.example: The village holds a summer fiesta.

definition_zh: 取来；接来；卖得（价钱）
definition_en: to go and bring something back, to go and get a person, or to be sold for a particular price
core_image: 狗叼着球从草地那头一路跑回来，尾巴甩得飞快
scene: 他把球扔出去，狗立刻跑过去叼了回来。The dog fetched the ball.
sceneCN: 这里 fetch 是「取来」（第 1 个义项）；句意：狗把球叼了回来。

senses.title: Go and bring back
senses.definition: to go to another place and bring something back
senses.definitionCN: 到另一处把某物带回来
senses.example: The dog fetched the ball.
senses.exampleCN: 狗把球叼了回来。
senses.why: This is the basic sense of going and returning.
senses.whyCN: 这是「去而复返」的基本义。

senses.title: Go and get a person
senses.definition: to go and bring a person to a place
senses.definitionCN: 去把某人带到某处
senses.example: Please fetch the doctor quickly.
senses.exampleCN: 请快去把医生请来。
senses.why: People can be fetched as well as objects.
senses.whyCN: 人也可以像物品一样被「接来」。

senses.title: Sell for a price
senses.definition: to be sold for a particular amount of money
senses.definitionCN: 以某个价钱被卖出
senses.example: The old clock fetched a high price.
senses.exampleCN: 那座旧钟卖了个好价钱。
senses.why: An object can fetch what buyers pay for it.
senses.whyCN: 物品能「卖得」买家愿付的价钱。

intro.en: Fetch comes from Old English feccan, to go and get.
intro.cn: fetch 源自古英语 feccan（去取来）。

items.en: Feccan meant to go and bring.
items.cn: feccan 意为去取回。

items.en: The verb appeared in everyday household use.
items.cn: 该动词常见于日常家务语境。

items.en: Fetch kept the idea of a round trip.
items.cn: fetch 保留了「往返一趟」的意思。

items.en: It came to mean to bring a person.
items.cn: 它开始表示把人带来。

items.en: Trade gave it the sense of selling for a price.
items.cn: 商业又赋予它「卖得价钱」的义项。

note.en: Fetch is compared with similar-looking words and with verbs of bringing.
note.cn: 把 fetch 与形近词以及表示「带来」的动词作比较。

entries.definition: to carry something to a place

normalIntro.en: Fetch means to go, get something, and come back.
normalIntro.cn: fetch 意为去、取到手，再回来。

normal.en: Fetch implies a round trip.
normal.cn: fetch 隐含往返一趟。

normal.en: A dog loves to fetch a ball.
normal.cn: 狗喜欢把球叼回来。

normal.en: To fetch a doctor is to go and bring one.
normal.cn: fetch a doctor 就是去把医生请来。

normal.en: A house can fetch a high price.
normal.cn: 房子可以卖个好价钱。

normal.en: Far-fetched means stretched too far to believe.
normal.cn: far-fetched 意为牵强到难以相信。

abstract.en: To fetch is to close a distance and return.
abstract.cn: 去取，就是消除一段距离再回来。

abstract.en: What a thing fetches is what someone will pay.
abstract.cn: 一件东西卖得多少，取决于有人愿付多少。

abstract.en: Some errands are small journeys of care.
abstract.cn: 有些跑腿，是小小的关心之行。

examples.en: The dog fetched the ball.

definition_zh: 很少的；不多的；少数

definition_zh: 田地；领域；场地；战场；派上场

definition_zh: 打架；战斗；斗争；斗志
definition_en: to use force against someone, to take part in a battle, to work hard for something, or the will to keep resisting
core_image: 拳击台上两人对视，汗水沿着下巴滴到地面
scene: 两个男人在街上动起手来。The two men started to fight in the street.

senses.title: Physical clash
senses.definition: to use physical force against someone
senses.definitionCN: 对某人使用武力

root: 源自拉丁语 figura（形状），出自 fingere（塑造），核心义「成形的样子」。

sensesIntro.en: Figure means a number, a person, a shape, a body form, or to think and calculate.
sensesIntro.cn: figure 意为数字、人物、图形、身材，或认为与估算。

core.en: A form that can be seen, counted, or thought about.
core.cn: 可以被看见、被计数或被思考的形态。

branches.en: Data expressed as numbers.
A person who stands out.
A drawn or printed shape.
The outline of a body.
The act of concluding.

intro.en: Figure belongs to the Latin family of shaping and form.
intro.cn: figure 属于拉丁语中表示塑造与形状的词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin figura and fingere are the historical base.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 figura 与 fingere 是历史词根。

items.example: The president is only a figurehead.

那个故事是臆造出来的。

definition_zh: 文件；档案；归档；排队行进
definition_en: a folder or set of papers, a collection of stored information, to store papers in order, or to walk in a line
core_image: 一叠纸被一根细线穿在一起，挂在墙上的钉子上
scene: 他打开文件，读起第一页。He opened the file and read the first page.
sceneCN: 这里 file 是「文件」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他打开文件，读起第一页。

senses.title: Document
senses.definition: a set of papers or data kept together
senses.definitionCN: 归在一起的一组纸质或电子资料
senses.example: He opened the file and read the first page.
senses.exampleCN: 他打开文件，读起第一页。
senses.why: This is the everyday sense of a document.
senses.whyCN: 这是文件最常见的意思。

senses.title: Stored record
senses.definition: a collection of records kept for reference
senses.definitionCN: 供查阅的档案记录
senses.example: The police keep the case on file.
senses.exampleCN: 警方把此案存档。
senses.why: Records are kept in a file for later use.
senses.whyCN: 记录被存进档案以备日后使用。

senses.title: To store in order
senses.definition: to put papers into a system or place
senses.definitionCN: 把文件放入系统或位置
senses.example: File the reports before Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 周五前把报告归档。
senses.why: The noun turns into the act of keeping it.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为保存它的动作。

senses.title: To walk in line
senses.definition: to walk one behind another
senses.definitionCN: 一个接一个地走
senses.example: The children filed into the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们排队走进大厅。
senses.why: A line of people resembles a string of papers.
senses.whyCN: 一列人就像一串文件。

intro.en: File comes from Latin filum, a thread, because papers were once strung on a line.
intro.cn: file 出自拉丁语 filum（线），因为旧时文件被穿在线上。

items.en: Filum meant a thread or string.
items.cn: filum 意为线或细绳。

items.en: Filare meant to spin thread.
items.cn: filare 意为纺线。

items.en: Filer meant to string papers on a line.
items.cn: filer 意为把文件穿在线上。

items.en: A file became a set of papers kept in order.
items.cn: file 变成按顺序保存的一组文件。

items.en: The word extended to computer files.
items.cn: 该词扩展到计算机文件。

note.en: File is compared with similar-looking words and with words for stored records.
note.cn: 把 file 与形近词以及表示存档记录的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: File is a thread of papers, a stored record, and a line of people.
normalIntro.cn: file 是一串纸、一份存档，也是一列人。

normal.en: Keep the contract on file.
normal.cn: 把合同存档。

normal.en: She filed the letters by date.
normal.cn: 她按日期给信件归档。

normal.en: The students walked in single file.
normal.cn: 学生们排成一列行走。

normal.en: A filename names a computer file.
normal.cn: 文件名给电脑文件命名。

normal.en: File a complaint means to report it formally.
normal.cn: file a complaint 意为正式提出投诉。

abstract.en: A thread can hold many pages into one story.
abstract.cn: 一根线能把许多页穿成一个故事。

abstract.en: Order is what turns paper into a file.
abstract.cn: 秩序把纸张变成档案。

abstract.en: A line of people moves at the speed of its first step.
abstract.cn: 一列人的速度取决于第一步。

examples.en: He opened the file and read the first page.
examples.cn: 他打开文件，读起第一页。

examples.en: The police keep the case on file.
examples.cn: 警方把此案存档。

examples.en: The children filed into the hall.
examples.cn: 孩子们排队走进大厅。

dict_mnemonic.text: file 出自拉丁语 filum（线），本义「把文件穿在线上保存」，后引申为文件、档案与排队行进。

root: 源自拉丁语 filum（线），核心义「用线串起、成序保存」。

sensesIntro.en: File means a document, a stored record, the act of storing, or walking in a line.
sensesIntro.cn: file 意为文件、档案、归档或排队行进。

core.en: Papers held together in order.
core.cn: 按顺序归拢在一起的纸张。

branches.en: Papers kept together.
Records kept for later use.
The act of putting papers away.
People moving one behind another.
A single file and a case file share one word.
branches.cn: 一份文件与一宗案卷共用一个词。

intro.en: File belongs to the Latin thread family, from which profile and filament also come.
intro.cn: file 属于拉丁语「线」词族，profile 与 filament 也出自这里。

latinIntro.en: Latin filum and filare are the historical base.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 filum 与 filare 是历史词根。

items.example: The files are in the drawer.
The profile shows a smiling face.

definition_zh: 装满；填补；充满；担任
definition_en: to make something full, to close a gap, to make someone feel a strong emotion, or to take a role
core_image: 水从壶口倾下，杯子一寸寸被注满
scene: 她把杯子倒满了水。She filled the glass with water.
sceneCN: 这里 filled 是「装满」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她把杯子倒满了水。

senses.title: Make full
senses.definition: to put something into a container until it is full
senses.definitionCN: 往容器里放东西直到满
senses.example: She filled the glass with water.
senses.exampleCN: 她把杯子倒满了水。
senses.why: This is the basic sense of making full.
senses.whyCN: 这是使某物变满的基本义。

senses.title: Fill a gap
senses.definition: to close or complete an empty space
senses.definitionCN: 堵住或补全空白
senses.example: Workers filled the hole with cement.
senses.exampleCN: 工人用水泥填平了洞。
senses.why: A hole is an empty space to be filled.
senses.whyCN: 洞就是等待填满的空处。

senses.title: Full of feeling
senses.definition: to make someone feel a strong emotion
senses.definitionCN: 使人产生强烈情感
senses.example: The news filled her with joy.
senses.exampleCN: 这个消息让她满心欢喜。
senses.why: Emotion can fill a person like water.
senses.whyCN: 情感能像水一样充满一个人。

senses.title: Take a role
senses.definition: to take a position or do a job
senses.definitionCN: 担任职位或从事工作
senses.example: She filled the empty seat on the board.
senses.exampleCN: 她补上了董事会的空缺席位。
senses.why: A vacant role is a space to be filled.
senses.whyCN: 空缺的职位就是一个待填的位置。

intro.en: Fill comes from Old English fyllan, to make full, from full.
intro.cn: fill 源自古英语 fyllan（使满），出自 full。

items.en: Full meant having no empty space.
items.cn: full 意为没有空隙。

items.en: Fyllan meant to make something full.
items.cn: fyllan 意为使某物变满。

items.en: Fillen covered containers and holes.
items.cn: fillen 既指装满容器也指填洞。

items.en: Fill in and fill out name the act of completing forms.
items.cn: 英语中用 fill in 与 fill out 表示填写表格。

items.en: Refill means to fill again.
items.cn: refill 意为重新装满。

note.en: Fill is compared with similar-looking words and with words for loading a space.
note.cn: 把 fill 与形近词以及表示装入空间的词作比较。

entries.definition: to put things into a container
to take up a space or role

normalIntro.en: Fill means to make full, close a gap, flood with feeling, or take a role.
normalIntro.cn: fill 意为装满、填补、充满情感或担任。

normal.en: Fill the bottle with clean water.
normal.cn: 把瓶子装满干净的水。

normal.en: Fill in the form in black ink.
normal.cn: 用黑色墨水填写表格。

normal.en: A good meal fills the room with warmth.
normal.cn: 一顿好饭让满屋温暖。

normal.en: She filled the role of guide.
normal.cn: 她担任了向导的角色。

normal.en: Refill means to fill the cup again.
normal.cn: refill 意为再把杯子装满。

abstract.en: A hole is a chance for something to fill it.
abstract.cn: 空洞正是某物来填补的机会。

abstract.en: Feeling can fill a room without a sound.
abstract.cn: 情感可以无声地充满房间。

abstract.en: A role waits to be filled by someone willing.
abstract.cn: 一个角色等着愿意的人来担任。

examples.en: She filled the glass with water.
examples.cn: 她把杯子倒满了水。

examples.en: Workers filled the hole with cement.
examples.cn: 工人用水泥填平了洞。

examples.en: The news filled her with joy.
examples.cn: 这个消息让她满心欢喜。

dict_mnemonic.text: fill 源自古英语 fyllan（使满），出自 full，本义「使容器变满」，后扩展为填补、充满情感与担任。

root: 源自古英语 fyllan（使满），出自 full，核心义「使变满」。

sensesIntro.en: Fill means to make full, close a gap, overwhelm with feeling, or take a role.
sensesIntro.cn: fill 意为装满、填补、充满或担任。

core.en: Empty space becoming full.
core.cn: 空处被填满。

branches.en: A container reaching its limit.
An empty space closed up.
Emotion rising to the brim.
A position taken by someone.
What makes full also makes whole.

intro.en: Fill belongs to the Germanic full family.
intro.cn: fill 属于日耳曼语中表示「满」的词族。

latinIntro.en: Fill has no Latin ancestor; Latin plenus and implere are semantic parallels.
latinIntro.cn: fill 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 plenus 与 implere 只是语义对应。

items.meaning: the act or something that fills
items.example: The filling is made of fruit.

definition_zh: 电影；胶片；薄膜；拍摄
definition_en: a motion picture, a thin strip of material for recording images, a thin layer, or to record something with a camera
core_image: 放映机的光穿过胶片，在墙上投出晃动的画面
scene: 我们昨晚看了一部关于海洋的电影。We watched a film about the ocean last night.
sceneCN: 这里 film 是「电影」（第 1 个义项）；句意：我们昨晚看了一部关于海洋的电影。

senses.title: Motion picture
senses.definition: a story or record shown in moving pictures
senses.definitionCN: 以活动画面讲述故事或记录事物的作品
senses.example: We watched a film about the ocean last night.
senses.exampleCN: 我们昨晚看了一部关于海洋的电影。
senses.why: This is the most common modern sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是现代最常见的义项。

senses.title: Photographic strip
senses.definition: a thin strip coated to record images
senses.definitionCN: 涂有感光层、用于记录影像的薄带
senses.example: The old camera still uses film.
senses.exampleCN: 这台旧相机仍使用胶片。
senses.why: Moving pictures were once recorded on film.
senses.whyCN: 活动画面曾被记录在胶片上。

senses.title: Thin layer
senses.definition: a very thin layer of material
senses.definitionCN: 一层极薄的材料
senses.example: A film of oil covered the water.
senses.exampleCN: 水面上覆着一层油膜。
senses.why: The oldest sense is a thin skin or layer.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项就是薄皮或薄层。

senses.title: To record
senses.definition: to record something with a camera
senses.definitionCN: 用摄影机记录某物
senses.example: They filmed the whole ceremony.
senses.exampleCN: 他们拍摄了整场仪式。
senses.why: The material name becomes the action.
senses.whyCN: 材料名转化为动作。

intro.en: Film comes from Old English filmen, a thin skin or membrane.
intro.cn: film 源自古英语 filmen（薄皮、薄膜）。

items.en: Filmen meant a thin skin or membrane.
items.cn: filmen 意为薄皮或薄膜。

items.en: Film named a thin covering or haze.
items.cn: film 指薄薄的覆盖层或薄雾。

items.en: Photography gave film a light-sensitive strip.
items.cn: 摄影术使 film 指感光胶片。

items.en: Film came to mean a motion picture.
items.cn: film 进而指电影。

items.en: The verb means to record with a camera.
items.cn: 动词形式意为用摄影机拍摄。

note.en: Film is compared with similar-looking words and with words for movies and layers.
note.cn: 把 film 与形近词以及表示电影和薄层的词作比较。

entries.definition: the art or place of films
a thin layer over a surface

normalIntro.en: Film is a thin layer first, then a strip that carries pictures, then the pictures themselves.
normalIntro.cn: film 先是薄层，再是承载画面的胶片，最后指影片本身。

normal.en: A film can mean a movie.
normal.cn: film 可以指一部电影。

normal.en: Old cameras used film.
normal.cn: 旧相机使用胶片。

normal.en: Soap leaves a film on the glass.
normal.cn: 肥皂在玻璃上留下一层薄膜。

normal.en: The verb means to record.
normal.cn: 动词形式意为拍摄。

normal.en: A filmmaker makes films.
normal.cn: filmmaker 拍电影。

abstract.en: A thin layer can hold a whole world of light.
abstract.cn: 薄薄一层也能承载整个光的世界。

abstract.en: Pictures in motion turn time into a story.
abstract.cn: 活动的画面把时间变成故事。

abstract.en: Recording is a way of refusing to forget.
abstract.cn: 记录是一种拒绝遗忘的方式。

examples.en: We watched a film about the ocean last night.
examples.cn: 我们昨晚看了一部关于海洋的电影。

examples.en: The old camera still uses film.
examples.cn: 这台旧相机仍使用胶片。

examples.en: A film of oil covered the water.
examples.cn: 水面上覆着一层油膜。

dict_mnemonic.text: film 源自古英语 filmen（薄皮），本义「薄层」，后指感光胶片，再指电影与拍摄。

root: 源自古英语 filmen（薄皮、薄膜），核心义「薄薄的一层」。

sensesIntro.en: Film means a movie, a photographic strip, a thin layer, or to record with a camera.
sensesIntro.cn: film 意为电影、胶片、薄膜或拍摄。

core.en: A thin layer that can carry images.
core.cn: 能承载影像的薄层。

branches.en: A story told in moving pictures.

items.example: The scene has a filmic quality.

items.example: The records are stored on microfilm.
items.exampleCN: 这些记录存放在缩微胶片上。

definition_zh: 肮脏的；污秽的；下流的；令人厌恶的；（天气）恶劣的
definition_en: covered with dirt; extremely dirty; obscene or disgusting; used to describe very bad weather
core_image: 一只摸过下水道口的手，黑泥嵌在指纹里怎么搓都搓不掉
scene: 维修工从污水井里爬上来，手套上糊满黑泥，他皱着眉说。His gloves were filthy after he climbed out of the sewer.
sceneCN: 这里 filthy 是「肮脏的、沾满污垢的」（第 1 个义项：被脏东西覆盖）；句意是他从污水井爬出来后手套上全是污垢。

pos.zh: 肮脏的；污秽的；满是污垢的
下流的；猥亵的；道德败坏的
（口语）令人厌恶的；（天气）恶劣的

derivatives.zh: 由形容词性名词 filth 加形容词后缀 -y 构成 filthy；filth 本身义为「污物；秽语」
filthy 加名词后缀 -ness，义为「肮脏；污秽」
filthy 加副词后缀 -ly，义为「肮脏地；下流地」
与 filthy 同族的日耳曼源形容词，义为「难闻的；肮脏的」

senses.title: Covered with dirt
senses.definition: covered with or full of dirt and stains
senses.definitionCN: 被污垢、泥渍覆盖或沾满脏东西
senses.example: The floor was filthy after the dog ran through the mud.
senses.exampleCN: 狗踩过泥地之后，地板变得很脏。
senses.why: The word grew from filth, so the base picture is matter that clings to surfaces and refuses to come off.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从 filth（污物）长出来，核心画面是黏在表面上、怎么擦都擦不掉的脏东西。

senses.title: Extremely dirty in degree
senses.definition: so dirty that it shocks or disgusts people
senses.definitionCN: 脏到让人震惊或反感的程度
senses.example: The kitchen was filthy; even the cups had a layer of grease.
senses.exampleCN: 厨房脏得吓人，连杯子都蒙着一层油。
senses.why: Adding -y to filth intensifies it into an adjective of degree: not just dirty, but dirt itself made visible.
senses.whyCN: 在 filth 后加 -y 使之成为程度形容词：不只是「脏」，而是「污物本身显形」。

senses.title: Obscene or indecent
senses.definition: relating to sex in a rude or offensive way
senses.definitionCN: 以粗俗冒犯的方式涉及性，如低俗笑话或言语
senses.example: He told a filthy joke at dinner and everyone went silent.
senses.exampleCN: 他在晚饭时讲了个下流笑话，所有人都沉默了。
senses.why: Dirt applied to language: words treated as mental grime become obscene speech.
senses.whyCN: 把「脏」从物理挪到语言上：被视为心灵污垢的言语就成了下流话。

senses.title: Morally corrupt
senses.definition: morally bad or dishonest, especially for the sake of money
senses.definitionCN: 道德上恶劣或不诚实，尤指为钱财不择手段
senses.example: The novel describes a filthy merchant who cheats his own workers.
senses.exampleCN: 小说描写了一个欺压自己工人的卑鄙商人。
senses.why: Moral dirt is the metaphor: corruption of money and conduct is imagined as grime on the soul.
senses.whyCN: 这是「道德之脏」的隐喻：金钱与品行上的败坏被想象成灵魂上的污垢。

senses.title: Disgusting or unpleasant
senses.definition: very unpleasant, especially in taste, smell, or habit
senses.definitionCN: 非常令人不快，尤指气味、味道或习惯上的恶心
senses.example: The water in the bottle tasted filthy and warm.
senses.exampleCN: 瓶子里的水又温又恶心。
senses.why: Senses of touch, smell and taste share one channel with dirt, so disgust spills from one sense to all.
senses.whyCN: 触觉、嗅觉、味觉与「脏」共用同一通道，厌恶感由一个感官蔓延到全部。

senses.title: Bad weather
senses.definition: used about weather that is cold, wet and unpleasant
senses.definitionCN: 形容又冷又湿、令人难受的天气
senses.example: We stayed indoors all day because the weather was filthy.
senses.exampleCN: 天气恶劣，我们整天待在屋里。
senses.why: Rain and mud literally produce dirt, so foul weather is naturally called filthy.
senses.whyCN: 风雨泥泞确实会制造脏污，所以恶劣天气被顺理成章地称作 filthy。

senses.title: Extremely rich
senses.definition: informal, used in the phrase filthy rich about people with a great deal of money
senses.definitionCN: 口语用法，出现在 filthy rich 这一短语中，形容极有钱的人
senses.example: Her uncle is filthy rich but still drives an old car.
senses.exampleCN: 她叔叔富得流油，却仍开着一辆旧车。
senses.why: The older phrase filthy lucre linked money with moral dirt, and filthy rich keeps that ironic flavor.
senses.whyCN: 更早的 filthy lucre（不义之财）把金钱与道德之脏相连，filthy rich 保留了这种反讽味道。

senses.title: Overflowing or excessive
senses.definition: used about amounts of something unpleasant that are disgustingly large

intro.en: Filthy is the adjective of filth, a native Germanic word, and its history is unusually clean to trace: foul to filth to filthy.
intro.cn: filthy 是 filth 的形容词形式，filth 是日耳曼本土词，其词源脉络异常清晰：foul → filth → filthy。

items.en: The reconstructed root *fulaz meant rotten, corrupt or dirty; it gave related forms across Germanic languages.
items.cn: 重构形式 *fulaz 意为「腐烂的、败坏的、脏的」，在各日耳曼语言中产生同族词形。

items.en: Old English had ful meaning foul, and formed the noun fulth, dirt or refuse, with an abstract noun suffix.
items.cn: 古英语有 ful（污秽的），并用抽象名词后缀构成 fulth，义为「污物、秽物」。

items.en: The noun became filth, and by the twelfth century the adjective filthi appeared, meaning covered with filth.
items.cn: 名词演变为 filth，约十二世纪出现形容词 filthi，意为「沾满污物的」。

items.en: The extended senses developed: obscene language, morally corrupt conduct, and foul weather are all recorded in this period.
items.cn: 引申义在此时期出现：下流言语、道德败坏的行径、恶劣天气均有文献记载。

items.en: Today filthy covers dirtiness of body and place, foul speech, disgusting taste, bad weather, and the ironic phrase filthy rich.
items.cn: 如今 filthy 覆盖身体与场所的脏、污秽言语、恶心的味道、恶劣天气，以及带反讽色彩的 filthy rich。

note.en: These neighbors share spelling roots or dirty-weather meanings, and it is easy to mix them up.
note.cn: 下列词与 filthy 在拼写、同根或「脏、恶劣」义场上相近，容易混淆。

senses.exampleCN: 她在金融行业工作。
senses.why: This sense points to banks and investment.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项指向银行与投资领域。

senses.title: Public revenue
senses.definition: relating to the money of a government
senses.definitionCN: 与政府收支有关的
senses.example: The city faces a financial shortfall.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市面临财政短缺。
senses.why: Governments also manage money.
senses.whyCN: 政府同样要管理资金。

senses.title: Company accounts
senses.definition: relating to the money and accounts of a business
senses.definitionCN: 与企业的资金和账目有关的
senses.example: The company is in financial trouble.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司正陷入财务困境。
senses.why: A business keeps its own accounts.
senses.whyCN: 企业有自己的账目要管。

intro.en: Financial goes back to Latin finis, an end, through French finance, a payment that settles a debt.
intro.cn: financial 上溯至拉丁语 finis（结束），经法语 finance（结清债务的付款）演变而来。

items.en: Finis meant an end or a boundary.
items.cn: finis 意为终点或边界。

items.en: Finare meant to settle a debt.
items.cn: finare 意为结清债务。

items.en: Finance named a payment or revenue.
items.cn: finance 指付款或收入。

items.en: Finance came to mean money management.
items.cn: finance 进而指资金管理。

items.en: The adjective financial described money matters.
items.cn: 形容词 financial 用来描述资金事务。

note.en: Financial is compared with similar-looking words and with words about money.
note.cn: 把 financial 与形近词以及表示金钱的词作比较。

entries.definition: a person who deals in money

normalIntro.en: Financial is the adjective of finance, so it describes anything that involves money.
normalIntro.cn: financial 是 finance 的形容词，用来描述一切与金钱有关的事物。

normal.en: A financial crisis shakes the banks.
normal.cn: 金融危机让银行动荡。

normal.en: Financial aid helps students pay fees.
normal.cn: 经济援助帮学生支付学费。

normal.en: A financial adviser plans your money.
normal.cn: 理财顾问为你的钱做规划。

normal.en: The company reports financial results each year.
normal.cn: 公司每年公布财务业绩。

normal.en: Financial trouble means the money is short.
normal.cn: 财务困境意味着资金短缺。

abstract.en: Money is a promise that people agree to trust.
abstract.cn: 金钱是人们约定去信任的一种承诺。

abstract.en: A financial system turns trust into numbers.
abstract.cn: 金融体系把信任变成了数字。

abstract.en: Every account is a story of choices made.
abstract.cn: 每一本账目都是选择的故事。

examples.en: The company is in financial trouble.
examples.cn: 这家公司正陷入财务困境。

examples.en: She works in the financial sector.
examples.cn: 她在金融行业工作。

examples.en: They offered financial support to the family.
examples.cn: 他们向这家人提供了资金支持。

dict_mnemonic.text: financial 来自 finance（金融），加形容词后缀 -ial，表示「与资金有关的」。

root: 源自拉丁语 finis（结束），经法语 finance（结算、收入）演变为「财政、金融」。

sensesIntro.en: Financial describes matters of banking, public revenue, or company accounts.
sensesIntro.cn: financial 描述银行、政府收支或企业账目方面的事务。

core.en: Everything that belongs to money and its management.
core.cn: 一切属于金钱及其管理的事物。

branches.en: Belonging to banks and investment.
Belonging to government money.
Belonging to a company's accounts.
Both deal with large sums of money.
Public and private books share the word.
branches.cn: 公共与私人账目共用一词。

intro.en: Financial is built from the noun finance plus the adjective suffix -ial.
intro.cn: financial 由名词 finance 加形容词后缀 -ial 构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root finis, an end, also gave finish and final.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 finis（结束）也孕育了 finish 与 final。

items.exampleCN: 这个项目在财务上是稳健的。

items.example: The bridge was financed by the city.

items.exampleCN: 这位金融家资助了铁路。

latinEntries.example: Finis marks the end of a debt.
Finare meant to end a debt by paying.
latinEntries.exampleCN: finare 意为付款了结债务。
